title: Machine Learning Assisted Approach for Finding Novel High Activity Agonists of Human Ectopic Olfactory Receptors.
summary: Random-forest screening and docking prioritized candidates from five databases; luciferase assays identified two OR1A1 agonists and one OR2W1 agonist. These receptor-activation assays do not establish a therapeutic effect.
organization: Macquarie University; Duke University; Duke Medical Center

evidence.tested: Luciferase dose-response assays identified two OR1A1 agonists with EC50 95% confidence intervals of 11.5–24.4 and 12.2–25.0 μM, and 2-ethoxynaphthalene as an OR2W1 agonist with interval 3.05–6.59 μM. Benzophenone was the positive activation control. Other selected compounds were inactive or weak activators.
evidence.unknown: Only selected candidates were experimentally tested; classifier sensitivity and F1 scores were below 0.80. Receptor activation in this assay does not establish physiological or therapeutic effects.
evidence.ai_role: Random-forest classifiers trained on molecular descriptors ranked database compounds within training-like chemical space; docking helped select candidates for receptor luciferase assays.

source_review.scope: PMC primary abstract and indexed primary screening/luciferase Results including control and 95% EC50 confidence intervals; complete Methods not independently reviewed.
